section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic despatches, intelligence memoranda, cross-reference sheets, and intercepted reports from May 1943 to January 1944 examining Japan's deteriorating internal situation during World War II. Key subjects include the reorganization of the Tojo Cabinet, proceedings of the 82nd and 83rd extraordinary sessions of the Imperial Diet, sweeping industrial readjustment laws, severe shortages of metals and consumer rations, and shipping crises. The papers also assess peace sentiment among conservative Japanese elites, friction over policy toward the Soviet Union, factional politics within the Korean exile community, and post-war planning regarding the institution of the Japanese Emperor.

subfiles.about: An analysis of the political implications of Premier Hideki Tojo's cabinet reorganization, factional compromises, and Axis foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Analysis forecasts an IRAA-Assistance Political Association merger under Tojo's faction-balancing appointments, concluding his cabinet remains weak and compromise-driven, requiring close Allied/Soviet watching of Japan-Axis ties.
subfiles.title: Commentary on the Reorganization of the Tojo Cabinet and Axis Relations

subfiles.about: A report on living conditions, morale, air-raid preparations, commodity rationing, and industrial activity in Japan based on an interview with a departed Turkish diplomat.
subfiles.summary: American Consul Burton Y. Berry in Istanbul reports on an extensive debriefing of a reliable member of the Turkish diplomatic mission who departed Japan on April 1, 1943. The informant noted that Japanese public morale remained superficially high due to stringent censorship, although educated circles privately expressed grave doubts regarding ultimate victory against Anglo-American resources. The despatch details intensified air-raid precautions, strict rationing of sugar, flour, and meat, sharp reductions in clothing point allowances, flourishing currency and goods black markets, and expanding industrial development including synthetic oil plants. Observations are also provided on travel through Korea, Manchuria, and Siberia, noting high Soviet war morale and warm popular sympathy for Anglo-American visitors.
subfiles.title: Istanbul Despatch: Report on Current Conditions in Japan Based on Interview with Member of Turkish Diplomatic Party

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting a War Department transmittal of a Justice Department report on strategic objectives in Tokyo and postwar planning.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a 1943 War Department communication encloses Sadler's report on Tokyo-area strategic objectives and postwar planning.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Strategic Objectives in Tokyo Area and Postwar Planning Suggestions

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram requesting intelligence on merchant vessel construction in Korea and Japan during 1943.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a 1943 telegram relays a Board of Economic Warfare request for monthly Korea/Japan merchant-vessel launch data by shipyard.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Merchant Vessels Launched in Korea and Japan in 1943

subfiles.about: A memorandum reviewing and offering suggestions on Stephen Naft's booklet 'Japan's Menace to the Americas' for use in Inter-American radio broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Stabler forwards a critique of Naft's 'Japan's Menace to the Americas,' correcting oversimplifications on women and religion, suggesting propaganda highlight Japanese exploitation of the Philippine Catholic Church.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Suggestions in Regard to Stephen Naft's Booklet 'Japan's Menace to the Americas'

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording the Department of State's acknowledgment and observations regarding the report on Tokyo strategic objectives and postwar planning.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: State's reply to the War Department on Sadler's Tokyo strategic-objectives and postwar-planning report, submitting its own observations.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Strategic Objectives in Tokyo Area and Postwar Planning Suggestions

subfiles.about: A despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with General Wang Peng-sheng regarding the economic, political, and military implications of the extraordinary session of the Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires George Atcheson, Jr. transmits a memorandum of conversation between Embassy officer Carl H. Boehringer, General Wang Peng-sheng, and Dr. T. T. Mar on the significance of the extraordinary session of the Japanese Diet held June 16-18, 1943. General Wang emphasized that the session's primary achievement was the industrial readjustment bill, designed to convert machinery to war production, scrap obsolete equipment for shipbuilding metal, and suppress private plutocratic political influence. Wang estimated that 2,000,000 workers would be displaced with up to 75 percent remaining unemployed, an estimate Embassy officers considered improbable given Japan's acute labor shortage. The subfile includes a Division of Far Eastern Affairs summary memorandum by Johansen and an identical duplicate copy of the despatch and enclosure.
subfiles.title: Chungking Despatch No. 1365: Transmittal of Memorandum of Conversation in Regard to Significance of Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Diet, June 16-18, 1943

subfiles.about: A despatch forwarding a secret Chinese intelligence analysis on the 82nd Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Diet, peace sentiment, and the risk of war with Soviet Russia.
subfiles.summary: George Atcheson, Jr. transmits a secret study prepared by Dr. T. T. Mar, special assistant to General Wang Peng-sheng, analyzing the 82nd Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Diet and its relation to domestic and foreign policy. The report details Japanese anxiety over American industrial and shipbuilding power following Allied successes in the Solomons, prompting radical state-ownership controls over private industry. It reveals that a conservative clique linked to Prince Konoye advocates negotiated peace with Britain and America, while military radicals urge war against the Soviet Union, warning that a cabinet collapse might cause the Kwantung Army to attack Vladivostok. An attached memorandum of September 7, 1943, by Max W. Bishop of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs summarizes the document's key conclusions.
subfiles.title: Chungking Despatch No. 1377: Document entitled 'The 82nd Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Diet and its Relation to Home and Foreign Affairs'

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing a memorandum by John K. Emmerson concerning Japan's philosophy of life.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Emmerson's 1942 memorandum analyzing Japan's wartime philosophy of life and cultural attitudes.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japan's Philosophy of Life

subfiles.about: A despatch transmitting a Polish intelligence report on Japanese policy disorientation and shifting strategic attitudes following Mussolini's downfall.
subfiles.summary: Biddle forwards a Polish-intelligence report of a neutral-capital Japanese diplomat arguing Japan can't defeat Russia, should drop the Anti-Comintern Pact and pro-Axis generals, and seek Soviet-mediated China peace.
subfiles.title: London Despatch No. 397: Attaching Copy of Report Entitled 'Disorientation in Japanese Policy'

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing an additional reference to John K. Emmerson's memorandum on Japan's philosophy of life.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: additional filing reference for Emmerson's 1942 memo on Japan's philosophy of life.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japan's Philosophy of Life

subfiles.about: A confidential FBI communication regarding political disputes between Korean nationalist leaders Kim Koo and Kim Yak-san in Chungking.
subfiles.summary: Hoover relays FBI intelligence that Kim Koo attacked Kim Yak-san over Soviet collaboration before being reinstated, with a Chungking unity conference set for October 9.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter to Adolf A. Berle, Jr.: Political Significance of Resignation of Kim Koo

subfiles.about: A telegram summarizing a Soviet article analyzing Japan's economic crisis, political fissures, and diplomatic stratagems following the 83rd Diet session.
keywords: The War and the Working Class
subfiles.summary: Ambassador W. Averell Harriman transmits a detailed summary in two sections of an article by A. Ilin in 'The War and the Working Class' on the 83rd Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Diet. The Soviet author interprets Japanese domestic and foreign measures as symptoms of a profound national crisis driven by Allied industrial output, air-raid vulnerabilities, and economic strain. The article analyzes the establishment of the Ministry of Munitions under Tojo to enforce total economic mobilization, notes an emerging split between the government and fascist extremists underscored by the suicide of Seigo Nakano, and dismisses Foreign Minister Shigemitsu's 'Greater East Asia' peace offensive and puppet independence for Burma and the Philippines as desperate demagogy.
subfiles.title: Moscow Telegram No. 2034: Soviet Article on Results of the Eighty-Third Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Parliament

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 1823 from Chungking concerning representative official Chinese views on Japanese political affairs.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Chungking Despatch 1823 reports official Chinese opinion on recent Japanese political developments.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Representative Official Chinese Opinion in Regard to Recent Political Developments in Japan

subfiles.about: Correspondence between Professor George D. Hubbard and the Department of State regarding Hubbard's paper 'A Future for Japan'.
subfiles.summary: Hubbard asks State's view on publishing his paper 'A Future for Japan'; Spaulding thanks him but says the Department can't endorse private manuscripts.
subfiles.title: Correspondence regarding George D. Hubbard's Paper 'A Future for Japan'

subfiles.about: A despatch transmitting a Manchester Guardian article analyzing the postwar status of the Japanese Emperor and Emperor-worship.
subfiles.summary: Gallman forwards a Manchester Guardian article weighing using Emperor Hirohito as a postwar figurehead against Shinto militarism's dangers, noting Chinese calls to abolish the Tenno system.
subfiles.title: London Despatch No. 13363: Transmitting Article Entitled 'The Japanese Emperor'

subfiles.about: A despatch forwarding an OWI report on severe rationing, scrap metal collections, and merchant shipping sinkings in Nagasaki and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Gauss forwards Caldwell's OWI report: a Nagasaki informant describes strict rationing, metal shortages requisitioning bridge railings, and halted Nagasaki-Shanghai shipping from submarine losses, with Shanghai conditions even worse.
subfiles.title: Chungking Despatch No. 2033: Conditions in Japan and Shanghai Reported by John Caldwell

subfiles.about: An intelligence memorandum summarizing observations on living conditions, civilian morale, and shortages in Japan and occupied China gathered from American repatriates aboard the Gripsholm.
subfiles.summary: Langdon synthesizes Gripsholm repatriates' accounts: shifting Japanese morale toward grim defensiveness, falling urban living standards, weak wooden shipbuilding, and predatory Japanese requisitions fueling Chinese guerrilla resistance in occupied China.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on General Conditions in Japan and Occupied China by William R. Langdon

subfiles.about: A despatch transmitting a Manchester Guardian article by Gunther Stein analyzing Japanese fatalism and vulnerability to Allied bombing.
subfiles.summary: Fisher forwards Stein's article on a Chinese escapee's account of Japanese civilian fatalism, predicting early Allied bombing would demoralize the public against its own government rather than the Allies.
subfiles.title: London Despatch No. 13,574: Transmitting Gunther Stein's Article 'Japan from the Inside'
